summary: Two published CPI event-study articles were built on hard-coded release dates inferred from a 13th-of-month calendar proxy. Against the official FRED/ALFRED calendar, 7 of 13 dates were wrong and one was a release that never happened. Both articles' headline numbers reverse. Neither article can be repaired by editing numbers in place: the T-7 piece's central thesis is contradicted by its own corrected evidence, and it contains a fabricated event, an impossible release date, and a false provenance claim.

official_dates_used.source: FRED/ALFRED release calendar, release_id=10 (Consumer Price Index), via volpred.data.event_dates.cpi_release_dates
official_dates_used.independent_confirmation: FRED /series/vintagedates for CPIAUCSL — a different endpoint with no 'last release per month' dedup rule anywhere in it, which is what the release-calendar path cannot self-check. Per FRED's docs a vintage date is a date on which values were released OR revised, so this is a corroborating diagnostic, not a pure first-release oracle; its exact agreement here additionally assumes no extra revision vintages landed in the window. Returns an identical 12-date list.

phantom_release.finding: No CPI was published in November 2025 at all. The October-2025 reference month — which that November slot would have carried — was cancelled during the government shutdown.
phantom_release.verified_at_source: FRED series CPIAUCSL has no observation for 2025-10-01 (value is '.')
phantom_release.note: The release month (November) and the reference month (October) are distinct. Prior write-ups, including the docstring of src/volpred/data/event_dates.py, conflate them; see handoff notes.

official_dates_used.sample_size_change: 13 -> 12 (the phantom November release is gone). The T-2 'earlier 9' comparison group becomes 'earlier 8'.

independent_check.result: PASS — 198 checks. Every number the articles quote, except the T-7 bootstrap (consistency-checked only), reproduced along a separate implementation path.
axes: Event dates path A: raw ALFRED /release/dates with different params (desc sort, no include-with-no-data) and dict-based dedup instead of the module's groupby — catches an implementation bug in the module. Does NOT catch a shared conceptual error, since it applies the same last-per-month rule.

Event dates path B: /series/vintagedates for CPIAUCSL — different endpoint, no last-per-month rule. Covers the failure mode path A cannot: a shared conceptual error in that dedup rule. All three agree. (Caveat: vintage dates cover releases OR revisions, so this corroborates rather than independently defines the release list.)
Phantom-release premise asserted directly at source: CPIAUCSL 2025-10-01 == '.'.

Reactions and event windows: recomputed with different pandas idioms (pct_change / shift + reindex) instead of the scripts' index.get_loc()/iloc walk — catches implementation bugs such as the ratio-window wrong-bound defect. LIMIT: this is NOT a non-positional cross-check. Series.shift(n) moves by row count exactly as pos+offset does, so both sides share the premise that 'N trading days later' == 'N rows later'. That premise is covered separately by the XNYS session check below, not by date agreement.

VIX session integrity validated against the XNYS exchange calendar — this is what actually tests the 'N rows = N sessions' premise. It caught a second phantom: yfinance returns a ^VIX quote for Memorial Day 2026-05-25, when NYSE and CBOE were closed. Both analysis scripts now drop non-session rows. Verified to change zero reported numbers (primary_numbers byte-identical before/after): ^VIX9D lacks that row so the ratio series already excluded it via index intersection, and all 12 events precede it.

NOT independently reimplemented: the T-7 block bootstrap. It is seeded (20260717) and reproducible by rerunning the script; the verifier checks only its presence, well-formedness, and internal consistency (p<0.05 iff |observed| > the absolute 95% critical value, which share one tail definition by construction).

reconciliation_with_published_errata.issue: The already-published errata article mile_9560b9cc (2026-07-12) reported the official-dates CPI-day VIX mean as -0.847%. This rerun reports -1.90% for the T-7 study. Both are correct; do not 'fix' one to match the other.
reconciliation_with_published_errata.explanation: Different windows. mile_9560b9cc runs through the 2026-06-10 release; the T-7 article (published 2026-05-26) could not have contained it. This rerun deliberately holds the original data window fixed so the before/after diff is attributable to the dates alone.
reconciliation_with_published_errata.arithmetic: 12 events mean -1.90% + the 2026-06-10 release at VIX +11.83% = 13 events mean -0.847%. Verified: the extended-window recompute returns -0.847% exactly.

articles.title: 🌡️ 事件溫度計｜US CPI 2026-06-13 預覽（T-7）：VIX 當日反應是抽籤，term structure 才是訊號
articles.narrative_reversal_detail: The article's top-level conclusion ('CPI-day VIX reaction is unpredictable / not significant') technically survives — the corrected mean is still not significantly different from zero (t p=0.113; sign test p=0.146). But every number supporting it reverses, and the corrected data leans the opposite way: 9 of 12 releases saw VIX fall, versus the 7-up/6-down 'coin flip' the article reported. This is a conclusion that was right for entirely wrong reasons.
articles.severity_reason: Beyond wrong numbers, the article contains three factual defects: it announces a release date that falls on a Saturday, it reports and narrates an event that never happened, and it twice claims a data provenance ('CPI 發布日期據 BLS 官方行事曆') that is false. Sentence-level number edits cannot fix these.

factual_errors.note: 2026-06-13 is a SATURDAY. BLS does not release on weekends. The article's premise was impossible on its face.

factual_errors.new: must be removed or made true
factual_errors.note: FALSE PROVENANCE CLAIM. The dates were a 13th-of-month guess, not the BLS calendar. This is the most serious honesty defect in the piece.
A whole narrative paragraph is built on a cancelled release. The +14.2% and +32.1% are real market moves on a day that was not a CPI day.

factual_errors.old: 下一篇 T-2 預覽（預計 2026-06-11 發布）

new_values.direction_split: 3 up / 9 down (sign test two-sided p=0.146 — leans down, not significant at N=12)
new_values.ratio_ttest_caveat: IID/equal-variance assumption against an autocorrelated daily baseline; understates SE. Retained only for comparability with the original run.
new_values.ratio_bootstrap_spec: null-imposed stationary block bootstrap (Politis & Romano 1994), 10000 reps, geometric mean block 5 trading days, seed 20260717. Each replicate resamples the FULL ratio series and reapplies the same fixed CPI mask, preserving both the serial dependence and the ~monthly event spacing. Cite THIS for any significance claim, not the t-test.

articles.title: VIX 一根長腳之後：CPI 前夕的短端結構告訴我們什麼
articles.narrative_reversal_detail: The article argued reactions are NOT stably converging ('事件反應在「收斂、但偶爾炸一次」之間擺盪，不是穩定收斂'), citing recent-4 sigma 8.37% > earlier-9 sigma 6.53%. With official dates the opposite holds and significantly so: recent-4 sigma 0.69% vs earlier-8 sigma 4.46%, F=36.24, one-sided p=0.0067. Note the article's own reported F-test (p=0.7995) never supported its 'compression' framing either — the corrected data supports it.
articles.severity_reason: The 6/5 VIX spike spine of the article is date-independent and survives intact. But the entire recent-4 table, the reaction-trend narrative, the dispersion conclusion, and the pre-event run-up section all reverse. The two 'big jumps' the trend narrative rests on were not CPI reactions at all.

Byte-identical, and correctly so: this chart plots the VIX/VIX9D term structure and never touches event dates. Its being unchanged is a scope check — the fix landed exactly where it should and nowhere else.

Three of the four scripts wrote to /Users/yhlai0911/Desktop/volpred-research/..., a repo path that no longer exists. Those scripts could not run at all today — the artifacts on disk predate the repo move. This is why the brief's 'output path drifts with cwd' framing understates it: the paths were not cwd-relative, they were absolute and dead.

reruns.why: Extending the data would confound 'we fixed the dates' with 'we added fresh data'. Holding the original window makes the before/after diff attributable to the date source alone, which is what an errata must isolate.
reruns.codex_review: see README.md in each evidence dir
reruns.method_deltas_disclosed: Both packs disclose their method deltas in evidence.json errata_rerun. Neither claims 'method unchanged' — the event-session alignment was tightened (bidirectional +/-5-day nearest-match -> forward-only, bounded, fail-closed) and non-session rows are now dropped. Both are inert on this data and verified as such, but they are method changes and are listed as such.
